headline: Forty Eight Plays, One Hundred Ninety Five Dollars, Zero Alibis
paragraphs: Fifty six games got graded, twenty got waved off, thirty six drew action, and forty eight tickets went out at ten dollars each. Fourteen won. The week closed 14-32-2 for a loss of 195.23 on 480 staked, an ROI of negative 40.7 percent. The model walked in expecting 61.2 percent of these to land and delivered 30.4, which is roughly the gap between a forecast and a coin that hates you.

Spreads did the heavy damage at 8-21-1 and negative 137.28. Totals went 3-8-1 for negative 52.73 while claiming 65.1 percent confidence, the loudest number on the sheet and the least earned. Moneylines survived at 3-3 and negative 5.22, the betting equivalent of getting out of the building with your wallet. The published top five, the five the model was proudest of, went 1-4 against a stated 69.9 percent expectation and lost 30.91. Negative 61.8 ROI on the flagship.

Two calls at nearly identical conviction tell the whole story. Over 40.5 in Miami (OH) at Central Michigan hit at 28-27, a 7.5 point edge that cashed 9.09. Over 43 in Michigan State at UCLA, a 7.4 point edge rated at the same 71 percent, watched a 28-10 final and died. Lines moved on 43 plays and six moved toward the model, 14 percent, so the market was not confused about any of this. Season sits at 134-173-8 across five real weeks, down 416.50, negative 13.2 ROI. The only profitable stretch on the books is a 40-25-1 week graded in hindsight for plus 110.47, which is to say the model is undefeated at picking games it already watched.
Nothing further. The table is right there.
